chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn Abdullah, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said:

I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Upon me is the fasting of a month if my uncle comes out of prison.' So he came out. I woke up in the morning intending to fast, and one of our companions came to me. So I called for the midday meal and ate with him. He said, 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem/It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Does eating during the day invalidate a specific vowed fast if interrupted by a guest?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the ruling of a conditional vow (nadhr) to fast for a month upon a specific event, establishing its obligatory nature once the condition is met. It further provides practical jurisprudential guidance, confirming that breaking the fast for a necessary meal due to a companion's visit does not invalidate the vow, highlighting the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding social obligations and vows.
